newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Women troubled by low status in Cambodian society.
newsitem.headline: Women troubled by low status in Cambodian society.

text.p: Cambodians held several gala commemorations this week ahead of International Women's Day on Saturday, but many women said their plight cast a shadow on celebrations.

"We are very sorry that at present, there are some Khmer women, especially teenagers and minors, who are victims and mistreated," said Princess Bopha Devi, reading a statement from Queen Norodom Monineath during a ceremony at Olympic Stadium.
She cited prostitution and sex abuse as particular problems.

Women's rights workers said that despite the fact that women represent 53 percent of wage earners and head one in four households, they have few opportunities for equal rights, including education and top jobs.
Recent census figures show women complete on average only 2.6 years of school, compared to five years for men.
"Working women in Cambodia", a report from the Asian American Free Labor Institute (AAFLI), recently found that economic gains in Cambodia were undermined by women workers' deteriorating rights.
That situation apparently extends to the home, with one in six women estimated to be physically abused by their husbands, according to a survey last year.
"The status of women in Cambodia is very low, so that exacerbates the problem of domestic violence," Robin Mauney of the Project Against Domestic Violence, told Reuters.

Activists said the week's commemorative events, including separate ceremonies led by co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen, needed to be carried over into concrete action to improve women's rights.
A proposal by Ranariddh earlier this week to give women a 30 percent quota in the National Assembly received a lukewarm reception.
"We need a change in attitude, not quotas," said one women's rights worker. "We don't need to force it, we just need to let skilled women climb the ranks of government."
